W1-1.note: The hands moved freely, every part was sound, the Sunday winding was blank, and the clock started at once when wound; the electric works were only proposed, never adopted.

W1-2.note: The notebook's Sunday line was blank and the narrator had the key with them at a friend's house; pins, cable, hands and nests are all explicitly ruled out.

W1-3.note: Petra spoke first about the bus leaving forty minutes late and asked how soon the clock could be trusted; someone else raised safety, and Jonas raised the cost.

W1-4.note: To strike a bargain is to conclude or settle one; 'sounded' tempts because of the clock and bell setting.

W1-5.note: The ending is told in flat, matter-of-fact sentences with no comment on events (paid as agreed, key returned, summer stacking tins), though a reader could argue for quiet regret since the narrator caused the stoppage.

W1-6.note: The last page showed a blank line for Sunday, which is how the missed winding was found.

W2-1.note: Only the hand-pollinated plots set seed, and the passage concludes the starwort was simply short of bees.

W2-2.note: Petra Moss, the warden, blamed the late frosts, and so did Brisk.

W2-3.note: The plan is for Hale to spend next July on the slope with his paintbrush, and the grant pays to keep him there.

W2-4.note: The grant will cover the cost, meaning pay for it.

W2-5.note: The author praises the board for moving quickly and changing course gracefully, which is plainly admiring.

W2-6.note: The passage says outright that the photograph is what brought Varga up the ridge in 2023.
